implementation: Public writer wrapper indexes each dictionary once by (slice, source-group index).
Existing writer body is renamed without indentation or numerical changes.
ConvertFromDictionaryToArray selects the requested lookup group; a direct private writer call without a cache follows the old full scan.
ThreadStatic restricts the cache to the output thread; finally releases all references after each public call.
memory_tradeoff: One KeyValuePair snapshot per sparse entry, typically 24 bytes of payload before Lookup group overhead and array capacity slack; no added full-grid cache.
complexity: Dictionary filtering becomes O(entries) per output call instead of O(entries * source groups * slices); dense buffer clearing, compression and file output are unchanged.
static_evidence: Program.cs:625-638 waits for the previous output thread before the next dispersion cycle.
Program.cs:724 returns from ParallelParticleDriver before Program.cs:777-778 starts the writer thread.
VolumeCorrection occurs before the writer thread, so grouped values include the same correction.
Each dictionary key is unique; group enumeration writes unique array locations and does not sum or reorder arithmetic.
risks: Additional sparse snapshot memory may outweigh the time benefit for tiny outputs.
This remains a local diagnostic prototype; no claim of native parity or performance is made before root testing.
Lookup construction precedes the old writer exception handling; catastrophic allocation failure can propagate from the wrapper.
test_recommendations: Strict Release build with warnings treated as errors.
Native comparison for large sparse 99-group, 9-slice output and ordinary 26-group output.
Transient multi-weather output with zero emissions in the middle situation to test cache lifetime.
Native odour with center/upper/lower populated; compare all three output formats plus ASCII and unzipped output.
Reflection direct writer fallback and full public wrapper paths; repeat two public calls on one thread with different dictionary contents.
Peak process commit and working set, not just managed allocation, because Lookup adds sparse snapshots.
alternatives: Removing ThreadStatic saves one attribute but would share cache state across output threads and focused tests. Passing cache through every private writer requires a wider signature change. Current wrapper approach confines the prototype to this file.
